summary: Multipronged billing offsets caused by stale rate-cache hits on edge postbacks
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Lumenly Inc. reports unexpected adjustment lines on their month-to-date invoice after a rate-tier change was deployed. Several provisional credits applied earlier in the cycle flipped to negative adjustments during nightly reconciliation. Impact: customer-facing revenue lines showed a net negative on their provisional invoice and triggered an autopay hold alert.

Impact:
- 3 invoice lines reversed for Lumenly (account ID hidden for PII) totaling ~USD 27,450 provisional variance.
- Autopay hold generated; customer requested immediate explanation and provisional waiver.

Environment and context:
- Rate-tier update deployed (pricing-service v2.14.0) at 2026-03-09T23:58:00Z.
- Edge proxy fleet in us-east had a rolling restart 2026-03-09T23:56–00:30 UTC.
- Postback-reconciler replays occurred during nightly reprocessing window 2026-03-10 02:00–03:00 UTC.

Why it's surprising: billing system is expected to consistently classify postbacks by the timestamp on the usage payload to apply the correct rate tier; here some postbacks were classified with pre-change tiers while others used post-change tiers, producing offsetting credits and negative adjustments.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy a rate-tier update to pricing-service (v2.14.0) with deploy window overlapping edge-proxy restart.
2) Send a batch of postbacks from an edge instance that still has stale pricing-cache (simulate by freezing pricing-cache refresh for 60s).
3) Allow postbacks to land in async postback queue and then trigger reconciler reprocessing for the same time window.
4) Observe that reconciler produces both pre-update and post-update attributions for the same usage timestamps, leading to provisional credit + reversal lines on invoice preview.
logs: 2026-03-10T02:12:08Z reconciler WARN detected duplicate-window for customer=lumenly postback_group=pg_441
2026-03-10T02:12:12Z reconciler INFO reprocessed postbacks count=183 classification=post-change
2026-03-10T02:12:15Z billing-engine ERROR invoice-delta generation produced negative_adjustment_line id=adj_774
comments: Support (Asha): Acknowledged with customer at 2026-03-10 04:05 UTC. Customer is requesting provisional waiver until root cause identified.
Customer (Lumenly - Maya R.): We saw the negative line on the preview and autopay was put on hold. Please advise whether this will be reversed; our AR team needs confirmation.

SRE (Diego): Reproducing locally with a cached pricing snapshot. Edge pods that restarted early sent postbacks with an old pricing-version header. Pinpointed two edge nodes with delayed cache invalidation.

Eng (Priya K.): Pricing-service change included a schema-compatible tier cutover; reconciler should have used usage.timestamp but used pricing-version header for classification in the presence of duplicates. Raising INT ticket for reconciler logic hardening.
Support (Asha): Coordinating provisional credit and customer communication. Finance contact CC'd for manual hold/waiver processing.
investigation_notes: Timeline constructed from deploy logs and reconciler traces. Root contributors identified: (1) pricing cache expiry race on edge proxies during rolling restart, (2) postback-reconciler logic preference for an incoming pricing-version header when deduplication window is active, and (3) asynchronous reprocessing that applied a newer pricing tier to a subset of postbacks leading to offsetting credit and charge lines. Sample repro created with a 45s pricing-cache freeze reproduces negative adjustment pattern locally. Related internal issue created INT-4421 to change reconciler to deterministically use usage.timestamp -> pricing cutover lookup and ignore pricing-version header for replays.
resolution_notes:
Short-term: finance applied a provisional waiver for the USD 27,450 net variance for Lumenly (waiver ID FW-2026-03-11-LUM). Support communicated waiver to customer and removed autopay hold pending cleanup (customer notified 2026-03-11 10:20 UTC).

Mid-term: engineering deployed reconciler patch (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/pricing/pull/2147) to prefer authoritative timestamp-based lookup for replay windows and added a sanity-check to detect mixed-classification in a single reconciliation batch; patch rolled out 2026-03-11T18:40:00Z.

Long-term: SRE will add a post-deploy edge-cache reconciliation step in the deploy playbook to avoid stale pricing-header forwarding during pricing changes. Also scheduling a billing postmortem and a customer-facing summary to be posted to Confluence.

Follow-ups: INT-4421 (reconciler code hardening), ENG-PR-2147 (merged), FIN-ops processed waiver. Customer billing statement will be reconciled in the next billing cycle and finance confirmed no further action required.
